messages:
Anna (SRE): paging — auth-validate is spiking 5xx and 429s, started ~14:02 UTC. Traffic from a small set of IPs, weird token reuse patterns. Seeing lots of validation failures with identical token prefixes. Suspect token exfil/replay.

Anna (SRE): sample log snippet: 
```
[2026-06-12T14:02:17Z] auth-validate ERROR token=eyJhbGci... client_id=svc-web-123 src=54.12.34.56 reason=invalid_sig
[2026-06-12T14:02:18Z] auth-validate WARN replay_attempts=34 src=54.12.34.56 session_id=7f3b...
[2026-06-12T14:02:19Z] auth-validate INFO token_prefix=eyJhbGci payload_mismatch=1 src=52.14.77.203
```

Anna (SRE): paging @oncall. Impact: increased 5xx -> downstream retries, some customer requests failing with auth errors. No confirmed data exfil yet but token holder behavior looks automated.

incident-bot: Incident created — sev2: "auth token replay suspects". Paging: Ben (oncall).

Ben (oncall): ack — I'm on it. Pulling logs and opening a mitigation plan. Can someone scope the CIDRs hitting auth?

Anna (SRE): top srcs: 54.12.34.56, 54.12.35.10, 52.14.77.0/24. ~78% of the spike from those ranges.

Ben (oncall): first actions: 1) block egress/ingress from the obvious CIDRs at LB/WAF; 2) revoke all active sessions for client svc-web-123; 3) rotate svc-web-123 client secret and rotate internal JWT signing key if needed. I'll coordinate.

Liam (Infra): I can push a quick WAF rule and a firewall deny for 54.12.0.0/16 now. Applying with short TTL. Will use emergency change so we can revert.

Ben (oncall): running session revocation command now:
```bash
# revoke sessions for service client
redwoodctl auth revoke-sessions --client svc-web-123 --reason "suspected token replay" --force
```

deploy-bot: deploy started: auth-revoker v2.1 -> staging -> prod (changes: bulk session revoke).

Jess (Security): +1 on revocation and CIDR block. Also: 1) we need forensics snapshot of logs (do not rotate away audit logs yet), 2) generate list of customer tokens potentially impacted, 3) prepare a key rotation window for svc-web-123 and a service-to-service JWT signing key. Avoid immediate global key swap until we have mitigation to avoid double-failures.

Jess (Security): Forensics query suggestion: 
```sql
SELECT timestamp, src_ip, client_id, token_prefix, action FROM auth_logs WHERE token_prefix IN (SELECT token_prefix FROM auth_logs WHERE replay_attempts > 10) ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 5000;
```

Anna (SRE): forensics export created to /s3-incidents/1794567890/ for Security. Audit retention pinned for 30 days.

Liam (Infra): WAF rule applied, firewall deny created: block-54-12 (TTL 4h). Early telemetry: 60% reduction in offending traffic.

Ben (oncall): rotated svc-web-123 secret (new secret uploaded to vault), updated service account and rolled out small canary to dependent services. Also triggered key rotation plan for internal jwt-signing-key v3 -> v4 with canary rollout.

Ben (oncall): runbook step — notify CS for customer impact comms. @CS-Alex can you prep an outreach template and list of customers with recent failed auths?

CS-Alex: on it. Draft message ready in ~30m. Will flag any high-value customers for immediate phone contact.

Jess (Security): please DO NOT post raw log excerpts with tokens to public channels. Mask token prefixes in all comms. If you need to share logs externally, use sanitized exports.

Anna (SRE): monitoring: error rate (5xx) dropped by ~75% in the last 10m after block + revoke. Latency returned to normal for most routes but some dependent services still see auth failures while they pick up the new secret.

Ben (oncall): mitigation status summary for handoff:
- Blocked 54.12.0.0/16 at LB/WAF (temp rule).
- Revoked sessions for svc-web-123 (bulk revoke completed).
- Rotated svc-web-123 secret in Vault and initiated canary rollout.
- Forensics export created and pinned.
- CS notified and drafting customer communication.
- Security is scheduling JWT signing-key rotation with a canary plan.

Ben (oncall): handing off to Liam (Infra) for overnight watch and to complete any further infra-level hardening. Key actions for night: keep WAF block, monitor for new offending IPs, complete JWT rotation canary tomorrow morning, and ensure we have a freeze on unrelated deploys to auth.

Liam (Infra): ack. I'll take primary for overnight. Will extend firewall TTL if we see continued traffic. I'll also prepare a short playbook to quickly add/remove CIDRs.

Jess (Security): I'll keep working with Ben and Anna on the rotation schedule. We'll set a 02:00 UTC maintenance window if needed.

Ben (oncall): final note — customer impact so far: ~0.6% of requests from top 200 customers experienced auth failures during the spike window; CS will prioritize outreach. No confirmed PII exfil identified.

Ben (oncall): handing off. If anything new shows up, page Liam and ping me. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

Liam (Infra): logged handoff in pager duty and the incidence tracker: https://incidents.redwood.example/1794567890

incident-bot: Incident sev2 transitioned to "monitoring". Handoff complete.

Ben (oncall): closing thread on my side, will reopen if escalation required.
